steps.decide: Whether the record set is paginated, infinitely loaded or both, and why
How the current page, total and range are stated so the reader knows where they are
How the control behaves when there are 3 pages, 30 or 30 000
How page changes interact with the URL, focus and scroll
What the reader sees when the page they asked for no longer exists

rules.statement: Records are paginated when the reader needs to compare, cite or return to a row; infinite loading is reserved for feeds where position never matters.
The control always states the visible range and the total in text, because '1 2 3 … 40' alone never tells anyone how much data they are looking at.
Up to seven pages are shown as numbers; beyond that the control collapses to first/last plus a page field, and the page field accepts a typed number.
The page lives in the URL, focus moves to the results heading after a page change, and scroll returns to the top of the results rather than the top of the document.
If filters shrink the set below the requested page, the reader lands on the last available page with a note, never on an empty table that implies no data.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: the page number is the request id; a response for a page the reader has already left is discarded

motion.motion: the results dim over 120ms while the control keeps its size
the new rows fade in over 140ms
motion.reducedMotion: the rows swap instantly and the range is announced

motion.motion: the previous page stays and an inline note appears over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the note appears instantly above the unchanged page

motion.motion: the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.motion: the control returns to pending over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the control returns to pending instantly

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: Move through a long result set without losing the reader's place, and always say how much data lies on either side.
useCases: jump to page 12 of a filtered set
return to page 1 after reviewing the end
type a page number when the set has 400 pages
nicheDifferences: Operate tables are read comparatively, so position and total are information, not decoration
A pager that hides the total makes every estimate a guess
inputs: the total record count and how it is computed
how many pages exist and the page size
whether deep links must restore a page
whether the set changes while paging
anatomy: page numbers or a page field
an inline failure note that keeps the current page
styling: the control is one row aligned to the end of the table, 44 px targets
the current page is distinguished by weight and aria-current, not colour alone
the pager never wraps to two ragged rows
a11y: buttons have names like 'Page 12' and 'Next page'
the range text is a live region so a page change is announced
the page field is a real number input with a label
responsive: the pager collapses to previous/next plus the range under 640 px
the number row scrolls inside its own container if it must, never the page
tap targets stay at least 44 px
copy: an emptied page says 'That page is now empty — showing the last page'
errors say what failed and that the current page is unchanged
alternatives: a load-more button when the set grows while the reader reads
infinite scroll only for chronological feeds
an export when the reader needs every row
acceptance: the control states range and total in text
the current page is marked with aria-current and announceable
the page lives in the URL and survives a reload
a page change moves focus to the results heading
a page past the end lands on the last page with a note
failureCases: the total is missing so the reader cannot estimate
a page change resets scroll to the document top and the reader loses their filter bar
deep links to page 12 silently open page 1

refused.reason: individual page buttons become unavailable rather than the whole control
a cursor control is either present or absent; it is never rendered inert
